title: Introduce routing handshake checksum and regional admission guard to stop variant echo cascade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-03-09 we observed a multi-region routing loop that amplified fallback fanout and escalated to an incorrect model-variant being selected for a subset of requests. The incident caused elevated latency and increased token cost for affected customers and triggered degraded SLOs in EU-West and us-east-1 for ~45 minutes. This ticket captures follow-ups to prevent re-occurrence by adding deterministic routing handshake verification, region-level admission checks, and hardened policy snapshot convergence guards.
timeline: 2026-03-09 01:04 UTC - First elevated retry rate observed from EU-West region; alerts fired for backend latency SLOs
2026-03-09 01:08 UTC - Router service began escalating fallbacks to variant-compat modes; telemetry showed fanout from 3 -> 48 model hosts
2026-03-09 01:12 UTC - Cross-region re-route occurred: EU-West requests bounced to us-east and back due to mismatch in policy precedence; observed routing loop for specific user session segment
2026-03-09 01:28 UTC - On-call mitigation: temporarily disable cross-region fallback policy; traffic stabilized, latencies returned to baseline by 01:50 UTC
2026-03-09 03:00 UTC - Post-incident investigation started; initial hypothesis: stale policy snapshot + missing variant-compat handshake caused echo and unbounded fanout
root_cause: A race between policy snapshot propagation and local admission decision allowed a router node to accept a fallback route whose variant compatibility matrix did not match the origin region's expectation. The router applied a fallback that triggered a capacity fallback in the target region; the target region's router, seeing load and a different stale policy version, chose to route back, creating an echo. There was no per-request handshake or checksum ensuring variant mapping consistency, and our policy propagation lacked a quorum validation before activation.
mitigation_summary: Short-term: disabled cross-region fallback, rolled back recent policy TTL reduction, and increased logging to capture ROUTE_ECHO_DETECTED events. Medium-term: implement routing handshake checksum and a regional admission guard to validate incoming fallback decisions. Long-term: add policy-snapshot quorum enforcement and a TTL harmonizer so routers reject snapshots older than X seconds unless explicitly authorized.
action_items: Implement a lightweight routing handshake checksum: each routing decision includes a 32-bit checksum derived from variant mapping and model-flavor metadata; accepting routers must verify checksum matches their active mapping or reject with explicit NO_MATCH reason

Add a regional admission guard that validates incoming cross-region fallback proposals against a local compatibility table and capacity budget; proposals that exceed fanout caps will be rejected or downgraded
Introduce policy-snapshot quorum enforcement: policy rollouts must be acknowledged by >=2 replicas in a shard before being marked active for cross-region fallback decisions
Create TTL harmonizer: enforce minimum snapshot freshness window (configurable) and record snapshot origin/sequence in telemetry
Rate-limit fallback fanout with exponential backoff and a per-request circuit breaker that emits ROUTE_ECHO_DETECTED when a request is routed across regions >2 times
Enhance telemetry and alerts: new alert RULE: ROUTE_ECHO_RATE > 0.5% for 5m triggers automated circuit-breaker activation and a runbook notification
Post-deploy chaos test: simulate policy propagation delay and capacity loss to validate that handshake and admission guard prevent echo formation
Document playbook and add to SRE runbooks: clear steps to disable cross-region fallback and safe rollback for policy snapshots
